key_insight: Modular surface-code QPUs can still perform fault-tolerant nonlocal logical operations even when interconnect Bell pairs are significantly noisier than internal qubits, and distributed GHZ preparation can be made much more resource-efficient.
engineering_relevance: This work gives design guidance for scaling quantum computers with noisy module-to-module links, showing that interface errors are less restrictive than expected and that ancilla/Bell-pair budgets can be reduced for distributed protocols.
method: Circuit-level simulations of logical nonlocal CNOT gates using lattice surgery between rotated surface-code QPUs connected by noisy Bell pairs
Evaluation of logical error rates under separate intra-QPU and interface noise models
Graph-based optimization for GHZ-state ancilla minimization, mapped to a vertex-cover problem with a polynomial-time heuristic
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that interfaces can tolerate noise up to about an order of magnitude higher than intra-QPU noise with only a minor threshold reduction, based on simulation-based logical error-rate analysis.
watch_item: The vertex-cover heuristic improves overhead, but real hardware performance will still depend on precise interface noise, Bell-pair fidelity, and control-synchronization details.
paper_title: Fault-Tolerant Logical Operations and Efficient State Preparation in Modular Quantum Architectures with Noisy Interfaces
